maria: quick thought 10 propose an "eviction cushion" mechanism: when a tenant briefly spikes, we temporarily move their hottest prefixes into a short-lived slab with higher eviction thresholds and shaped admission so we don't thrash the shared pool. this is local-only, no lease changes.

kevin: sounds useful. what are the key invariants we must preserve?

maria: ownership and lease tokens must be untouched. cushion only affects residency scoring, prefill concurrency, and admit pacing. also must ensure global memory accounting so we don't steal capacity from other tenants.

raj: how do we detect candidates? naive per-prefix hotness will be noisy. i suggest a hybrid: require both per-prefix hit-rate spike and tenant-level aggregate threshold over a sliding window. also include a minimum sustained duration to avoid flapping.

kevin: pseudo-detection:
```
hot_prefix = prefix.hit_rate > P_THRESH for window W1
tenant_hot = tenant.aggregate_hit_rate > T_THRESH for window W2
if hot_prefix && tenant_hot && sustained > MIN_DUR:
  mark_cushion(prefix, EXPIRE_TS)
```

maria: admission controls: cushion slab has its own soft credit pool. fills consume cushion credits; when pool is exhausted we throttle admits (not evict others). this prevents starving other tenants.

raj: good. corner-case: tenant with lots of tiny hotspots across many prefixes (one customer with many micro-services). quarantining all their prefixes could hog cushion. we should cap per-tenant cushion share and prefer top-k prefixes.

maria: agree10 prefer top-k by delta-hit-rate and cap total cushion memory per tenant. provide an opt-out tag for enterprise accounts that want to manage this themselves.

kevin: observability: emit events: cushion_enter, cushion_exit, credits_used, admits_throttled. tag fills and rehydrates with cushion=true for latency slicing. dashboard: cushion_active_tenants, cushion_memory_pct, tail-latency delta.

ops-bot: note: schedule read-only analysis run to compute cushion candidates on prod cluster tomorrow 03:00 UTC.

raj: rollout plan: 1) offline simulation with traces (include many small-tenant scenarios), 2) read-only candidate run for 48h, 3) 3% canary on read-write nodes, 4) expand if metrics okay. include kill-switch in ops console.

maria: unit tests: scoring path should have tests asserting no token/lease mutation; emulated multi-node race tests recommended.

kevin: perf: implementing cushion_boost increases residency; we need eviction accounting in the global allocator to respect cushion budgets. propose a soft pool backed by a reclaimable priority where cushion entries can be demoted when cluster-wide pressure crosses a threshold.

raj: action items:
- maria: write spec + small prototype PR for scoring and admission hooks
- kevin: build dashboards and read-only candidate job
- raj: run simulator with mixed traces and draft runbook
- ops: prepare canary and kill-switch

maria: will open PR tomorrow. any objections?

kevin: +1. keep scope local to eviction/residency layer only.
